mainTopic: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's דרשה on 'דברי חכמים כדרבנות', the story explaining why the students hesitated, and the signs of a שוטה.
overview: This amud finishes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's teaching that Israel is one unique nation. It then gives his דרשה on 'the words of the wise are like goads.' Torah guides like a goad, stays firm like a nail, and keeps growing like a plant. The many disagreements of the תלמידי חכמים all come from one Shepherd, so a student should open his ears to every side. רבי יהושע praises him: a generation with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is not orphaned. The גמרא asks why the students hesitated to share these teachings. It answers with a story: רבי אליעזר harshly punished a student who reported a 'new' vote about מעשר עני in עמון and מואב during שביעית. That ruling was really a הלכה למשה מסיני. Finally, a new topic begins: the signs of a שוטה. רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue whether all the signs or just one is needed, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing verse: Israel as one unique nation
steps.stepSummary: The previous דרשה of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה ends with a פסוק showing that הקב"ה made Israel one unique nation in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And who is like Your people, Israel, one nation in the land?"
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of the previous teaching. The גמרא brings the פסוק that proves ה׳ made Israel His one special nation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous teaching, Israel declared ה׳ unique, and ה׳ in turn declared Israel unique. This פסוק is the source for the second half: Israel is 'one nation in the land.' With this line the earlier דרשה is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: One nation; a single, unique people
Like Your people

phrases.english: "And who is like Your people, Israel,
one nation in the land?"

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the previous דרשה, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ made Israel His one unique nation.

steps.title: Torah is like a goad that guides you to life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה opens a new דרשה on a פסוק in קהלת. Just as a goad steers a cow to plow and produce food, Torah steers its learners from death to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also opened and taught: 'The words of the wise are like goads, and like firmly planted nails are the masters of assemblies; they were given from one shepherd.' Why is Torah compared to a goad? Just as a goad directs a cow to its furrows to grow food for the world, so Torah directs its learners from the paths of death to the paths of life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה begins a new teaching. He quotes a פסוק and explains its first picture: Torah is like a goad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goad is a sharp stick that pushes a cow to plow straight, and the plowing grows food that keeps the world alive. Torah does the same for a person. It nudges him off the road of death and onto the road of life. This first comparison sets up the rest of the דרשה, which goes through the פסוק word by word.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened and expounded; began a public teaching
A goad, a pointed stick for prodding an animal
Were compared
Its furrows, the lines a plow cuts in a field

steps.whatToRemember: Torah is not just information. Like a goad, it pushes a person in the right direction, toward life.

phrases.english: And he too opened and expounded:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the one who taught the previous דרשה.

phrases.english: "The words of the wise are like goads,
and like nails firmly planted
are the masters of assemblies;
they were given from one shepherd."
Why are words of Torah compared to a goad?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה דָּרְבָן זֶה מְכַוֵּין אֶת הַפָּרָה לִתְלָמֶיהָ
phrases.english: just as this goad directs the cow to its furrows
to bring forth life for the world,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְכַוְּונִין אֶת לוֹמְדֵיהֶן
phrases.english: so too words of Torah direct those who learn them
from the paths of death to the paths of life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second, separate דרשה by the same תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah guides its learners from the ways of death to the ways of life, the way a goad guides a plowing cow.

steps.title: Is Torah movable like a goad?
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is pushed further. A goad is a loose stick that gets moved around, so maybe Torah is also not fixed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as a goad is movable, maybe Torah is also movable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the goad comparison. If Torah is like a goad, maybe it is also loose and changeable like a goad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison can carry unwanted features with it. A goad is carried from place to place and is never fixed. That could suggest that Torah is not permanent, which would be a wrong idea.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then just as...
Movable; can be carried around

phrases.english: If so, just as this goad is movable,
so too words of Torah are movable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the goad comparison from step 2 can be taken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If Torah is like a goad in one way, maybe it is like a goad in every way, including being loose and changeable.

steps.title: The word 'nails' shows Torah is fixed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק also says 'nails.' A nail is fixed firmly in place, so Torah is permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Nails.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the next word in the פסוק. Torah is also compared to nails, and a nail stays fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second picture in the פסוק fixes the weakness of the first one. A goad guides, and a nail stays firmly in place. Together they teach that Torah both guides us and stays permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; the פסוק comes to say
Nails

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Nails."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second image in the same פסוק balances the first one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah might be loose and changeable, like a goad.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah is fixed and permanent, like a nail.

steps.title: Does Torah shrink like a nail?
steps.stepSummary: Now the nail comparison is tested. A nail wears away over time and never grows, so maybe Torah also gets less and never grows?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as a nail gets smaller and never grows, maybe Torah also gets smaller and never grows?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the nail comparison the same way it tested the goad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nail is fixed, which was good, but it also only wears down and never gets bigger. That might suggest that Torah slowly fades and never grows. The גמרא needs to remove this wrong idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A nail
Gets less and does not increase

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה מַסְמֵר זֶה חָסֵר וְלֹא יָתֵר —
phrases.english: If so, just as this nail gets less and does not grow,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חֲסֵירִין וְלֹא יְתֵירִין,
phrases.english: so too words of Torah get less and do not grow?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה מַסְמֵר זֶה חָסֵר וְלֹא יָתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the nail comparison from step 4 can be taken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A nail only wears down, so the comparison might imply that Torah only shrinks and never grows.

steps.title: The word 'planted' shows Torah grows
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the nails are 'planted.' A plant grows and multiplies, so Torah keeps growing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Planted.' Just as a plant grows and multiplies, so too words of Torah grow and multiply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the next word, 'planted.' Torah is like a growing plant, not a shrinking nail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נטועים is related to נטיעה, a plant. So Torah is firm like a nail but alive like a plant, and it keeps producing new learning. Each image fixes the weakness of the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Planted; firmly set in place
A plant or young tree
Grows and multiplies

steps.whatToRemember: Goad, nail, plant: Torah guides us, stays firm, and keeps growing.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Planted."
Just as this plant grows and multiplies,
so too words of Torah grow and multiply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another word in the same פסוק corrects the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah might shrink over time, like a nail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah grows and multiplies, like a plant.

steps.title: Scholars learning in groups and disagreeing
steps.stepSummary: 'Masters of assemblies' means תלמידי חכמים who learn in many groups. They often disagree: impure or pure, forbidden or permitted, invalid or valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Masters of assemblies': these are Torah scholars who sit in many groups and busy themselves with Torah. Some say impure and some say pure, some forbid and some permit, some declare invalid and some declare valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה moves to the next phrase in the פסוק and explains who the 'masters of assemblies' are. It also describes how these groups disagree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בעלי אסופות is read as groups of scholars learning together. The דרשה openly admits that they reach opposite conclusions on טומאה, איסור, and validity. This prepares the worry in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of assemblies; scholars who gather in groups
Torah scholars
Declare impure and declare pure
Declare invalid and declare valid

phrases.english: "Masters of assemblies":
these are Torah scholars,
who sit in many groups
and busy themselves with Torah.
These say impure and these say pure,
these forbid and these permit,
these declare invalid and these declare valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'masters of assemblies' are תלמידי חכמים who learn in groups and often reach opposite conclusions.

steps.title: How can anyone learn with so many disagreements?
steps.stepSummary: A person might feel lost. With so many opposite opinions, how can he learn Torah at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a person will say: How can I learn Torah from now on?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a natural worry that comes from all the disagreements. This sets up the final answer of the דרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one חכם says pure and another says impure, a learner may think Torah is confusing or that only one side can be real Torah. The question is whether learning Torah still makes sense when the scholars disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps a person will say
From now on; given this situation

phrases.english: Perhaps a person will say:
How can I learn Torah from now on?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a worry caused by the disagreements described in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the scholars disagree (step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Opposite rulings seem to make Torah study confusing or pointless for the learner.

steps.title: All opinions come from one Shepherd
steps.stepSummary: The end of the פסוק answers the worry: all the opinions were given by one shepherd. One God gave them and one leader, משה, said them, as the פסוק says 'God spoke all these words.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'They were all given from one shepherd.' One God gave them, one leader said them, from the mouth of the Master of all creation, blessed be He, as it is written: 'And God spoke all these words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry with the last words of the פסוק, 'from one shepherd.' All the opinions come from the same Source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when חכמים disagree, they are all working from the Torah that one God gave through one leader. The פסוק in שמות says 'all these words,' and this is brought to show that all of it came from ה׳. So the disagreements are part of one Torah and do not break it apart.

keyTerms.meaning: One shepherd, meaning ה׳
Leader of the people
Master of all creation
As it is written

steps.whatToRemember: The disagreements of the חכמים do not make Torah confusing. All the opinions come from one God, through one leader, משה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic idea for anyone learning גמרא: the many opinions in a מחלוקת are all part of Torah learning, because they all come from the same Source.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that every practical ruling is followed at once. It means that all sides of the discussion are words of Torah that come from ה׳.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "They were all given from one shepherd."
One God gave them,
one leader said them,

phrases.aramaic: מִפִּי אֲדוֹן כׇּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: from the mouth of the Master of all creation, blessed be He,
as it is written:
"And God spoke all these words."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The end of the same פסוק shows that all the opinions share one Divine Source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: So many opposite opinions might make Torah study confusing or impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the opinions were given by one God through one leader, so all of them are Torah and worth learning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Torah guides, stays firm, and grows. Even its many disagreements all come from one Shepherd.

steps.title: Make your ears like a funnel
steps.stepSummary: Because all the opinions come from one God, a student should listen to every side and work to understand each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: So you too, make your ears like a funnel and get yourself an understanding heart. Listen to those who say impure and those who say pure, those who forbid and those who permit, those who say invalid and those who say valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה ends with a practical lesson for the student. Since all the opinions come from one source, he should take in all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 removed the worry that Torah is falling apart. Now we hear what the student should do. He should not shut out one side. He should listen to every view and work to understand it. The same three pairs from step 7 (impure or pure, forbidden or permitted, invalid or valid) come back here, now as things to listen to.

keyTerms.meaning: A funnel or hopper. It is wide on top so everything poured in goes through.
An understanding heart, a mind that thinks through what it hears
Those who say invalid / those who say valid

steps.whatToRemember: Many opinions are not a reason to give up. All of them came from one source, so a student's job is to hear and understand all of them.

phrases.english: So too you, make your ears like a funnel,
and acquire for yourself an understanding heart to hear

phrases.aramaic: אֶת דִּבְרֵי מְטַמְּאִים וְאֶת דִּבְרֵי מְטַהֲרִים,
phrases.english: the words of those who say impure and the words of those who say pure,

phrases.aramaic: אֶת דִּבְרֵי אוֹסְרִין וְאֶת דִּבְרֵי מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: the words of those who forbid and the words of those who permit,

phrases.aramaic: אֶת דִּבְרֵי פוֹסְלִין וְאֶת דִּבְרֵי מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.english: the words of those who say invalid and the words of those who say valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer from step 9 into a practical instruction for the student.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Listen to every side of a debate and work to understand it, because all of it is Torah from one source.

steps.title: רבי יהושע praises רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: After hearing these teachings, רבי יהושע says that a generation with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is not orphaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: With these words he said to them: A generation is not orphaned when רבי אלעזר בן עזריה lives among it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע reacts to everything the students reported. He praises רבי אלעזר בן עזריה very highly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'orphaned' generation is one with no real leader or guide. רבי יהושע says that as long as רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is there, the generation has a true teacher. This closes the whole report of the דרשות the students brought from the בית המדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphaned generation, a generation with no leader
Lives among it, is present in it

phrases.english: In these words he said to them:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהושע, talking to the students who brought him these teachings.

phrases.english: A generation is not orphaned

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.english: when Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya lives among it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע responds to the full set of דרשות, ending with step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A generation that has רבי אלעזר בן עזריה has a true leader.

steps.title: Why didn't the students say it right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the students held back at first instead of telling רבי יהושע the teachings openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they should have just told him directly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the story. Why did the students hesitate before telling רבי יהושע what was taught?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story the students did not share the new teaching at first, and רבי יהושע had to push them. The גמרא asks why. Sharing Torah is good, so they should have spoken up right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, directly
But they should have told him

phrases.english: But let them say it to him directly?
phrases.notes: This points back to the start of the story, where the students held back until רבי יהושע pushed them to tell him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the drashos to ask about how the students behaved.
steps.kashyaTarget: The students' hesitation before reporting the teachings to רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be no reason to delay sharing Torah with one's teacher, so the hesitation needs an explanation.

steps.title: Because of something that once happened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the students were careful because of an earlier event, and it brings a ברייתא to tell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that happened, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: something happened before that made students careful. This line sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not stated as a rule. It points to a real event. The word דתניא tells us a ברייתא is coming to tell that event, and the story will show why the students were afraid.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident that happened

phrases.english: Because of an incident that happened. As it was taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and introduces the story that explains it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a past event that explains why they were careful
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was no reason for the students to hold back.
steps.terutzMaskana: A past incident taught them to be careful when presenting a new teaching to a great sage.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks what was new today
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית visits רבי אליעזר in לוד, and רבי אליעזר asks him what new thing was taught in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית, who went to greet רבי אליעזר in לוד. רבי אליעזר asked him: What new thing was taught in the בית המדרש today?
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins. A student visits his teacher, and the teacher asks what new idea was taught that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question רבי יהושע asked his students in our story. So the reader is set up to see what happened the other time a student answered it.

keyTerms.meaning: To greet, to pay a visit of respect to a teacher
Something new, a new teaching
The study hall

phrases.english: An incident with Rabbi Yosei ben Durmaskit
who went to greet
Rabbi Eliezer in Lod.
phrases.notes: Some versions have רבי אלעזר, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: He said to him: What new thing
was there in the study hall today?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא promised in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching was taught in the בית המדרש that day

steps.title: The vote about עמון and מואב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reports that the sages voted that in עמון and מואב, people separate מעשר עני in the שמיטה year.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: They counted votes and decided that in עמון and מואב, people separate מעשר עני in the שמיטה year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his teacher's question. He reports a new ruling the sages reached by voting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמון and מואב are next to ארץ ישראל but are not part of it. So the sages had to decide which מעשר applies there in the שמיטה year. They took a vote and ruled it is מעשר עני. The words 'they voted' will matter in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted votes and decided
The tithe given to the poor
The seventh year, the שמיטה year

phrases.english: He said to him: They voted and concluded:
In Ammon and Moab, they tithe
the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's question from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sages voted that עמון and מואב separate מעשר עני in the שמיטה year.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's angry reaction
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר angrily tells רבי יוסי to catch his eyes, and רבי יוסי's eyes are blinded.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יוסי, stretch out your hands and catch your eyes. He stretched out his hands and caught his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר reacts with sharp anger to the report, and his words come true: רבי יוסי loses his sight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the frightening event that explains step 13. A student reported a 'new' teaching and was punished. That is why the students in our story were careful before telling רבי יהושע. The גמרא will soon explain what bothered רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Stretch out your hands
Catch your eyes, as if they were falling out

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר disagreed with the ruling itself. The next step shows he agreed with it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yosei,
stretch out your hands and catch your eyes.
phrases.notes: Your eyes are about to fall out, so get ready to catch them. It was a curse of blindness.

phrases.english: He stretched out his hands and caught his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: יוֹסֵי, פְּשׁוֹט יָדֶיךָ וְקַבֵּל עֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר's reaction to the ruling reported in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reporting the 'new' ruling brought a harsh reaction. That shows why students were careful.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר weeps and quotes a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר cries and quotes the פסוק 'The secret of God is with those who fear Him,' showing the sages reached the right ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר wept and said: 'The secret of God is with those who fear Him, and He makes His covenant known to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: After his anger, רבי אליעזר cries. He quotes a פסוק about God revealing His secrets to those who fear Him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק means the sages who voted reached the true answer, guided by heaven, even if they did not know its source. So רבי אליעזר's anger was not because the ruling was wrong. He agreed with the ruling itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The secret of God is with those who fear Him
His covenant, to make it known to them

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar wept and said:
phrases.notes: This is the same sage from לוד that רבי יוסי visited. The name is written אלעזר here.

phrases.english: "The secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him,
and His covenant, to make it known to them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the angry reaction of step 16 and shows that רבי אליעזר agreed with the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sages' vote reached the true answer, because God reveals His secrets to those who fear Him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר confirms the vote with a tradition from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells רבי יוסי to go tell the sages not to worry, because their ruling matches a הלכה למשה מסיני he received through רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go tell them, do not worry about your vote. I received this from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who heard it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher: it is a law given to משה at Sinai that עמון and מואב separate מעשר עני in the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר sends a message back to the בית המדרש: their vote was correct. It is an old tradition going all the way back to Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 he cried because the sages reached the right answer on their own. Now he says exactly why it was right: it is not a new rule at all, but a הלכה למשה מסיני passed down from teacher to teacher. So the sages have nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: Your counting, meaning the vote the sages took
I have received this as a tradition
A law given to משה at Sinai and passed down by word of mouth
The seventh year, the שמיטה year

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling the sages reached by vote can turn out to match an ancient tradition from Sinai.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go say to them:
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר is speaking to רבי יוסי, and 'them' means the sages in the בית המדרש.

phrases.english: Do not worry about your vote,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מְקּוּבְּלַנִי מֵרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: this is what I received from Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
who heard it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher:
It is a law given to Moshe at Sinai

phrases.aramaic: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: that in Ammon and Moav they separate the poor man's tithe in the seventh year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ, לֵךְ אֱמוֹר לָהֶם: אַל תָּחוּשׁוּ לְמִנְיַינְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 17: after crying that the sages were right, רבי אליעזר now tells them their ruling is a tradition from Sinai.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר עני in עמון and מואב during שביעית is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Why these lands were left without the holiness of the land
steps.stepSummary: The reason is given: cities conquered by those who left Egypt lost their holiness, and those who returned from Babylonia left them unconquered so the poor could rely on them in the seventh year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt but were not conquered by those who came up from Babylonia. The first holiness was only for its time, not forever. They left those cities alone so the poor could rely on them in the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The text asks why עמון and מואב separate מעשר עני in שביעית, and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness from the first conquest, by those who came from Egypt, did not last forever. When the Jews returned from Babylonia, they chose not to conquer these cities again, so the land there was not holy and could be farmed in שביעית. Since it was farmed, מעשר עני was taken there, and the poor had food during the year off.

keyTerms.meaning: Large walled cities
Those who came up from Egypt, the first Jews to enter the land
Those who came up from Babylonia, the Jews who returned to build the second בית המקדש
The first holiness of the land, from the first conquest
For the future, meaning forever

steps.confusionAlert: The cities were not 'forgotten'. The returning Jews left them out on purpose, so the poor would have produce and מעשר עני to rely on in שביעית.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Those who came up from Egypt conquered many cities
but those who came up from Babylonia did not conquer them,
because the first holiness made it holy only for its time
and did not make it holy for the future,
and they left them alone
phrases.notes: 'They' means those who came up from Babylonia, who chose not to conquer these cities.

phrases.english: so that the poor could rely on them in the seventh year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה טַעַם — הַרְבֵּה כְּרַכִּים כָּבְשׁוּ עוֹלֵי מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the הלכה למשה מסיני stated in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do עמון and מואב separate מעשר עני in שביעית?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The returning Jews left those cities unholy on purpose, so they could be farmed in שביעית and the poor could rely on their מעשר עני.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's eyes are healed
steps.stepSummary: Once רבי אליעזר calmed down, he prayed that רבי יוסי's eyes be restored, and they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: After his mind settled, he said: May it be God's will that יוסי's eyes return to their place. And they returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends happily. רבי אליעזר calms down and prays, and רבי יוסי can see again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the story from step 16, where רבי יוסי was blinded. It also finishes the ברייתא brought in step 13 to explain why the students were careful about reporting new teachings to their teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind settled, he calmed down
May it be God's will, the opening of a prayer

steps.whatToRemember: The students were careful because of this story: a student reported a 'new' teaching, and his teacher reacted strongly, even though the ruling was correct.

phrases.english: It was taught: After his mind settled,
phrases.notes: 'His' means רבי אליעזר, who had been angry in step 16.

phrases.english: he said: May it be God's will
that Yosei's eyes return to their place. And they returned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story: the blinding from step 16 is reversed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's sight is restored, closing the story that explained why the students were careful.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the signs of a שוטה
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins: the ברייתא defines a שוטה as one who goes out alone at night, and one who sleeps in a cemetery, and one who tears his clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who is a שוטה? One who goes out alone at night, one who sleeps in a cemetery, and one who tears his clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new subject. It brings a ברייתא that gives three signs of a שוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא gives three clear behaviors to identify a שוטה. It does not yet say whether one sign is enough or all three are needed. That question is the setup for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is mentally unstable and not responsible in הלכה
A cemetery
His clothing

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Who is a shoteh?
One who goes out alone at night,
and one who sleeps in a cemetery,
and one who tears his clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story is over, and the גמרא moves to a new topic: defining who counts as a שוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The signs of a שוטה are going out alone at night, sleeping in a cemetery, and tearing one's clothing.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue how many signs are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a person is a שוטה only if he shows all the signs together. רבי יוחנן says even one sign is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא said: Not until all of them happen together. רבי יוחנן said: Even with just one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how to read the ברייתא's list of signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the list as one package: you need all three signs at once. רבי יוחנן reads it as three separate signs: any one of them is enough. The dispute is about how strict the definition of שוטה is.

keyTerms.meaning: All at once, together
Even with one of them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רב הונא as listing three separate tests. In his view the signs work together: one sign alone is not enough, and only all of them together, בבת אחת, make a person a שוטה.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna said:
He is not a shoteh until all of them are present together,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even with one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ כּוּלָּן בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the ברייתא from step 21: must the signs all appear, or is one sign enough?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: all the signs are needed together. רבי יוחנן: one sign is enough.

steps.title: What exactly is the case: crazy behavior or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of behavior we are talking about. Either way, it seems that counting signs makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he does these things in a crazy way, then even one sign should be enough. If he does not do them in a crazy way, then even all of them together should not make him a שוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing on רב הונא's view, which requires all the signs together. It sets up a dilemma: either way, the number of signs should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the acts come from madness, one act should already prove it. If they do not come from madness, adding more sane acts proves nothing. So why would three signs be needed, as רב הונא says?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
In a crazy way, out of madness
A person who is mentally unsound and not legally responsible
One (here, one sign)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not attacking the ברייתא's list of signs. It is asking how adding up signs could change anything. That question mainly targets רב הונא, who says all of them are needed.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he does them in a crazy way,
then even with one sign he should also be a שוטה.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא עָבֵיד לְהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שְׁטוּת —
phrases.english: If he does not do them in a crazy way,
then even with all of them he should not be a שוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּעָבֵיד לְהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שְׁטוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic behind רב הונא's position from step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that all the signs are needed together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. If the acts are crazy, one act should be enough. If they are not crazy, any number of them should be meaningless. Either way, counting signs adds nothing.

steps.title: Each sign alone could have a sane excuse, but not all together
steps.stepSummary: The acts are crazy, but each one alone can be explained away. When all of them happen together, the excuses no longer work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where he does them in a crazy way. Still, about sleeping in a cemetery, we could say he does it so that a spirit of impurity will rest on him. About going out alone at night, we could say a fever grabbed him. About tearing his clothes, we could say he is lost in thought. But since he did all of them, they become [signs of a שוטה].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma in defense of רב הונא. Each act alone could have an innocent explanation, but the combination of all of them cannot be explained away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer finds a middle option. The behavior looks crazy, but a single act still leaves room for a normal reason. Three different excuses for three different acts is too much to believe, so together they prove he is a שוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; it opens a defense of the original position
One could say, perhaps
A spirit of impurity
A kind of fever
A person lost in heavy thoughts or worries

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב הונא's rule is about proof. One odd act can be explained, but a pattern of acts shows real madness.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָא עָבֵיד לְהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שְׁטוּת,
phrases.english: Really, it is where he does them in a crazy way,
but the one who sleeps in a cemetery:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה עָלָיו רוּחַ טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: one could say that so a spirit of impurity will rest on him
is why he does it.
And the one who goes out alone at night:
one could say a fever grabbed him,
phrases.notes: He may simply be going out to cool down in the night air.

phrases.english: and the one who tears his clothing:
one could say he is a man lost in thought.
But since he did all of them,
they become…

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָא עָבֵיד לְהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שְׁטוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 23 by defining a middle case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the acts look crazy, but each one alone is open to a sane explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the acts are crazy, so one is enough, or they are sane, so none count
steps.terutzMaskana: Each act alone can be excused, but all of them together cannot, so רב הונא needs all the signs
